medium: Always-L with the visually observed position and breath-hold succeeds for every patient. Therefore body-build judgment and exposure economy affect only the optional perfect rating, not case completion; the four-unit budget never constrains this two-unit one-shot strategy.

The ALARA model equates a wider collimation field with two X-ray exposures. This communicates dose economy but is an oversimplified representation: field size changes irradiated volume and scatter, rather than literally converting one exposure into two.
Image adequacy judgment exists, but cutoff and blur are deliberately conspicuous and binary; there is limited room for progressively finer expert image-quality assessment.
low: The automated claim that position-aware L framing merely 'works' at a risk/reward cost understates the exploit: correct-position L deterministically covers all 27 generated cases.

The behavior harness exercises pure rules rather than rendered React interactions, so it does not verify rapid-click state-transition behavior, visual clipping fidelity, or whether children can reliably perceive the randomized build/posture cues.

CORE LOOP — inspect the patient, choose collimation, read the breathing cycle, expose, visually judge adequacy, then deliver or retake under a dose budget.
MASTERY — an expert matches position and minimum frame size, anticipates breath hold, rejects inadequate images without consulting the senior, and finishes with fewer exposures and retakes.
REPLAY — remounts or failed-case restarts generate different combinations of three builds, three positions, and three haze outcomes, allowing different economical framing decisions.

NOVICE VS EXPERT — novices can over-collimate, mistime, or misjudge an image; experts visually infer the matching position and smallest adequate field, time the hold, and recognize cutoff or motion blur.
recommended_actions: Make exposure economy consequential to completion, not only the perfect label—for example, use a multi-view or multi-patient dose budget where always-L leaves insufficient capacity.
Represent ALARA as relative dose or irradiated-area cost instead of counting a single wide exposure as two separate X-rays.
Add rendered-component tests for rapid clicks, randomized starting phases, clip-path output, and visible correspondence between rule geometry and the actual lung paths.
Strengthen the harness assertion for position-aware always-L to report its exact success rate and explicitly flag it as a completion-safe but inefficient strategy.
